question: The 'Kila Raipur Sports Festival', popularly known as the 'Rural Olympics', is traditionally held in which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kila Raipur Sports Festival (ग्रामीण ओलंपिक) is held annually near Ludhiana in Punjab, and began in 1933.

• It features rural sports such as bullock-cart races, tent-pegging, and feats of strength, celebrating Punjab's agrarian culture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Such traditional festivals are frequently asked in SSC exams by pairing them with their state: Kambala (buffalo race) – Karnataka; Jallikattu (bull taming) – Tamil Nadu; Kila Raipur (rural olympics) – Punjab.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 (Haryana), Option 3 (Rajasthan) and Option 4 (Gujarat) are incorrect; none of these hosts the Kila Raipur Rural Olympics, which is uniquely associated with Punjab.

question:
Arrange the following Delhi monuments in the correct chronological order of their construction (earliest to latest):

A. Tughlaqabad Fort

B. Qutub Minar (begun)

C. Alai Darwaza
solution_text:
The correct answer is B, C, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Qutub Minar was begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak (c. 1199) and completed by Iltutmish — earliest.

• The Alai Darwaza was built by Alauddin Khalji in 1311 as a gateway to the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque.

• Tughlaqabad Fort was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq (r. 1320-1325) — latest of the three.

• Correct sequence: Qutub Minar → Alai Darwaza → Tughlaqabad Fort, i.e., B, C, A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Dynastic order of the Delhi Sultanate: Slave/Mamluk (1206) → Khalji (1290) → Tughlaq (1320) → Sayyid (1414) → Lodi (1451). Anchoring monuments to their dynasty makes chronology questions easy.

 

NOTE

• Options placing Tughlaqabad Fort before the Qutub Minar or the Alai Darwaza are incorrect, as the Tughlaq structure is the most recent of the three.

question: Which of the following pairs relating to Mauryan administration is correctly matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitadhyaksha – Superintendent of Agriculture.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Arthashastra of Kautilya lists numerous 'adhyakshas' (superintendents) who ran specialised departments of the Mauryan state.

• Sita (सीता) referred to crown/state agricultural land; the Sitadhyaksha supervised agriculture on such land — correctly matched.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Correct pairings to remember: Panyadhyaksha – Commerce; Akaradhyaksha – Mines/Metals; Sunadhyaksha – Slaughterhouse; Pautavadhyaksha – Weights & Measures; Navadhyaksha – Shipping/Ports.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 wrongly links Panyadhyaksha (commerce) to mines; Option 2 wrongly links Akaradhyaksha (mines) to commerce; Option 4 wrongly links Sunadhyaksha (slaughterhouse) to ports — all are mismatched.

question:
Fill in the blank:

Jhaptaal, a taal commonly used in Hindustani classical music, consists of ____ beats (matras).
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A 'taal' (ताल) is the rhythmic cycle in Indian classical music, measured in beats called 'matras'.

• Jhaptaal has 10 matras, divided in a 2-3-2-3 pattern.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Beats of common taals: Teentaal – 16; Ektaal & Chautaal – 12; Jhaptaal – 10; Rupak & Keherwa (Keherwa is 8) ; Dadra – 6; Roopak – 7. Learning matra-counts is a recurring SSC music topic.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 (16) is Teentaal; Option 2 (12) is Ektaal/Chautaal; Option 3 (7) is Rupak taal — none corresponds to Jhaptaal, which has 10 beats.

question:
Fill in the blank:

In the sport of badminton, the height of the net at the centre of the court is ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.524 metres.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per BWF (Badminton World Federation) rules, the net is 1.55 m high at the posts and 1.524 m (5 feet) at the centre of the court.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Badminton facts often tested: court length 13.4 m; doubles court width 6.1 m; shuttlecock has 16 feathers; the sport's governing body is the BWF. India's premier badminton event is the India Open.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 (1.55 m) is the net height at the posts, not the centre; Option 2 (1.372 m) and Option 3 (1.20 m) are not standard badminton net measurements.

question: The famous rock-cut Kailasa Temple at Ellora, dedicated to Lord Shiva, was built during the reign of which Rashtrakuta ruler?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Krishna I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The monolithic Kailasa (Kailasanatha) Temple, Cave 16 at Ellora (Maharashtra), was carved out of a single rock during the reign of the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I (8th century CE).

• It is one of the largest rock-cut temples in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Rashtrakuta highlights: Dantidurga founded the dynasty; Amoghavarsha I authored 'Kavirajamarga' (earliest Kannada poetics) and built Manyakheta; Govinda III was a great conqueror.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 (Dantidurga) founded the dynasty but did not build the Kailasa temple; Option 3 (Amoghavarsha I) and Option 4 (Govinda III) reigned later and are not credited with the Ellora Kailasa temple.

question: Which of the following Governor-General and reform pairs is correctly matched?
option_2: Lord William Bentinck – Abolition of Sati (1829)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord William Bentinck – Abolition of Sati (1829).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord William Bentinck, aided by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, passed Regulation XVII of 1829 abolishing the practice of Sati (सती प्रथा).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Correct pairings: Lord Dalhousie – Doctrine of Lapse & first railway (1853); Lord Canning – Hindu Widow Remarriage Act 1856 (drafted under Dalhousie, enacted under Canning); Lord Ripon – First Factory Act & Local Self-Government (1882).

 

NOTE

• Option 1 wrongly credits Dalhousie with abolishing slavery; Option 3 wrongly links Cornwallis to widow remarriage; Option 4 wrongly links Ripon to the Doctrine of Lapse (that was Dalhousie's policy).

question: What is the standard distance of an Olympic marathon race?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 42.195 km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The official marathon distance is 42.195 kilometres (26 miles 385 yards), standardised by the IAAF (now World Athletics) in 1921.

• The distance traces back to the 1908 London Olympics, where the course was extended to end in front of the royal box.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Related athletics distances: a standard outdoor track is 400 m per lap; the steeplechase is 3000 m; the race-walk events are 20 km and (earlier) 50 km.

 

NOTE

• Options 41.195 km, 40 km and 42.5 km are not the standardised marathon distance, which is fixed at 42.195 km.

question:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option regarding Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

Assertion (A): INS Vikrant is regarded as a landmark in India's naval self-reliance.

Reason (R): INS Vikrant was constructed at the Cochin Shipyard Limited in Kerala.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• INS Vikrant (commissioned 2022) is India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier — so Assertion (A) is TRUE.

• It was indeed built at Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), Kochi — so Reason (R) is TRUE.

• However, the mere location of construction (CSL) does not by itself explain why it is a landmark in self-reliance; the landmark status stems from indigenous design and high domestic content. Hence R does not correctly explain A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• INS Vikrant is a Vikrant-class carrier (IAC-1), displaces about 45,000 tonnes, and operates MiG-29K fighters. It shares its name with India's first carrier (of 1961, of British origin).

 

NOTE

• Option 1 is wrong because R, though true, is not the correct explanation of A. Options 3 and 4 are wrong because both A and R are factually true.

question: The novel 'Tomb of Sand' (originally 'Ret Samadhi'), which won the International Booker Prize in 2022, was written by which author?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Geetanjali Shree.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Ret Samadhi' by Geetanjali Shree, translated into English as 'Tomb of Sand' by Daisy Rockwell, won the 2022 International Booker Prize.

• It became the first Hindi-language (and first Indian-language) novel to win the International Booker.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Indian Booker connections: Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize (1997) for 'The God of Small Things'; Kiran Desai won it (2006) for 'The Inheritance of Loss'; Aravind Adiga won it (2008) for 'The White Tiger'.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 (Arundhati Roy), Option 2 (Kiran Desai) and Option 3 (Anita Desai) did not write 'Tomb of Sand'; the novel is authored by Geetanjali Shree.

question: In December 2024, D. Gukesh became the youngest ever undisputed World Chess Champion by defeating which player in the final?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ding Liren.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the FIDE World Chess Championship 2024 held in Singapore, India's D. Gukesh defeated the reigning champion Ding Liren of China to become the 18th and youngest undisputed World Champion (at age 18).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Gukesh earned his title shot by winning the Candidates Tournament 2024. India's first World Champion in the classical format was Viswanathan Anand. In chess, FIDE is the international governing body.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 (Ian Nepomniachtchi) lost earlier world title matches to Carlsen and Ding; Option 2 (Magnus Carlsen) did not defend his title in 2024; Option 3 (Fabiano Caruana) was not Gukesh's final opponent.

question:
Which of the following statements about India's performance at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games is/are correct?

1. India won a total of six medals at the Games.

2. Manu Bhaker became the first Indian to win two medals at a single Olympic Games since independence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'Both 1 and 2 are correct'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's medal tally at the Paris 2024 Olympics was 6 medals — one silver and five bronze — so Statement 1 is correct.

• Shooter Manu Bhaker won two bronze medals (10 m air pistol individual and 10 m air pistol mixed team), becoming the first Indian to win two medals at a single Games in the post-independence era — so Statement 2 is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• India's lone silver at Paris 2024 came from Neeraj Chopra in the javelin throw. Overall it was one of India's larger medal hauls, driven by shooting.

 

NOTE

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because both statements are factually accurate, making 'Both 1 and 2' the correct choice.

question:
Fill in the blank:

Article ____ of the Indian Constitution abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 17.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 17, a Fundamental Right under 'Right to Equality', abolishes untouchability (अस्पृश्यता) and makes its practice in any form a punishable offence.

• It is enforced through the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Nearby Articles: Article 14 – equality before law; Article 15 – prohibition of discrimination; Article 16 – equality of opportunity in public employment; Article 18 – abolition of titles.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 (Article 18) abolishes titles; Option 2 (Article 19) grants six freedoms; Option 3 (Article 21) protects life and personal liberty — none deals with untouchability, which is Article 17.

question:
Read the following statements about mitochondria and choose the correct option:

1. Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration in the cell.

2. Mitochondria contain their own DNA and ribosomes.

3. Mitochondria are bounded by a single membrane.

Which of the above statements are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'Only 1 and 2'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mitochondria are the 'powerhouse of the cell', where aerobic respiration produces ATP — Statement 1 is correct.

• Mitochondria possess their own circular DNA and ribosomes, allowing partial self-replication — Statement 2 is correct.

• Mitochondria have a DOUBLE membrane (outer smooth, inner folded into cristae), not a single membrane — so Statement 3 is INCORRECT.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• The inner mitochondrial membrane folds (cristae) increase surface area for ATP synthesis. Because they carry their own DNA, mitochondria are explained by the endosymbiotic theory.

 

NOTE

• Options containing Statement 3 (i.e., 'Only 2 and 3', 'Only 1 and 3', and 'all three') are incorrect because the single-membrane claim is false — mitochondria have a double membrane.

question: Which of the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is correct?
option_1: The CAG audits the accounts of both the Union and the State governments
option_2: The CAG is appointed by the Parliament for a fixed term of six years
option_3: The CAG can be removed by the President at his own discretion
option_4: The CAG is a member of the Union Public Service Commission
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'The CAG audits the accounts of both the Union and the State governments'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Established under Article 148, the CAG audits all receipts and expenditure of the Union and the States, and of bodies substantially financed by government revenues.

• The CAG is the guardian of the public purse and heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• The CAG is appointed by the President and holds office for 6 years or until 65 years of age, whichever is earlier. Removal is by the same process as a Supreme Court judge (proved misbehaviour or incapacity), not at the President's discretion. CAG reports are examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC).

 

NOTE

• Option 2 is wrong (appointed by the President, not Parliament); Option 3 is wrong (removal follows the judge-removal procedure, not discretion); Option 4 is wrong (the CAG is not a UPSC member).

question: The 'Global Innovation Index' (GII), which ranks countries on their innovation capabilities, is published annually by which organisation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Global Innovation Index is published by WIPO, a specialised agency of the United Nations headquartered in Geneva.

• It assesses economies on innovation inputs and outputs such as institutions, human capital, research, and knowledge creation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Match reports to publishers: Global Competitiveness Report & Global Gender Gap Report – WEF; Ease of Doing Business (discontinued) & World Development Report – World Bank; Human Development Index – UNDP.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 (WEF), Option 3 (World Bank) and Option 4 (UNDP) publish other indices; the Global Innovation Index is a WIPO publication.

question: The 'Cheraw' dance, popularly known as the 'Bamboo Dance', is associated with which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cheraw is the traditional bamboo dance of Mizoram, in which dancers step rhythmically between bamboo staves clapped together by others.

• It is one of the oldest and most distinctive folk dances of the Mizo people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• North-East folk dances to remember: Bihu – Assam; Hojagiri – Tripura (Reang tribe); Wangala – Meghalaya (Garo); Bardo Chham – Arunachal Pradesh; Cheraw (bamboo) – Mizoram.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 (Meghalaya – Wangala/Nongkrem), Option 2 (Manipur – Manipuri/Thang-Ta) and Option 4 (Nagaland – various Naga dances) are associated with other dances, not Cheraw.

question: In the context of the Indian economy, what does 'Fiscal Deficit' represent?
option_1: The excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts
option_2: The excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings
option_3: The excess of total expenditure over total receipts including borrowings
option_4: The difference between primary expenditure and interest payments
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'The excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts (excluding borrowings).

• It indicates the total borrowing requirement of the government in a financial year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts. Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments. The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act aims to keep the fiscal deficit within targeted limits.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 defines the Revenue Deficit; Option 3 wrongly 'includes borrowings' (borrowings are what finance the deficit, so they are excluded); Option 4 relates to the Primary Deficit — none defines the Fiscal Deficit correctly.

question: What is meant by 'disguised unemployment' in an economy?
option_1: A situation where workers remain unemployed only during certain seasons of the year
option_2: A situation where educated persons are unable to find jobs matching their qualifications
option_3: A situation where more people are employed than are actually needed, so that the marginal productivity of extra workers is nearly zero
option_4: A situation where people voluntarily remain out of the labour force
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'A situation where more people are employed than are actually needed, so that the marginal productivity of extra workers is nearly zero'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In disguised unemployment (प्रच्छन्न बेरोज़गारी), the number of workers exceeds the requirement; removing some of them would not reduce total output.

• It is most common in the agricultural sector of developing economies, where family members share the same work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Related types: Seasonal unemployment (work only in certain seasons); Structural unemployment (skill-demand mismatch); Frictional unemployment (temporary, between jobs); Cyclical unemployment (due to downturns).

 

NOTE

• Option 1 describes seasonal unemployment; Option 2 describes educated/structural unemployment; Option 4 describes voluntary unemployment — none captures 'disguised' unemployment, defined by zero marginal productivity.

question: What is the primary objective of 'Mission LiFE', an initiative promoted by India at the global level?
option_1: To provide life insurance cover to all rural households
option_2: To generate employment through large infrastructure projects
option_3: To establish new thermal power plants for energy security
option_4: To promote an environment-friendly lifestyle and mindful, deliberate consumption
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'To promote an environment-friendly lifestyle and mindful, deliberate consumption'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) encourages individuals and communities to adopt sustainable, low-carbon behaviours and reduce wasteful consumption.

• It was proposed by India and highlighted at global climate platforms as a 'pro-planet people' movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Mission LiFE shifts the climate focus from 'mindless consumption' to 'mindful utilisation'. It complements India's climate goals, including the 'Panchamrit' commitments and the target of net-zero emissions by 2070.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 (insurance), Option 2 (infrastructure employment) and Option 3 (thermal power) misstate the mission; Mission LiFE is about sustainable individual lifestyles, not any of these.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Right to Constitutional Remedies:

1. Dr B.R. Ambedkar described Article 32 as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

2. During a National Emergency, the enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'Both 1 and 2'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution — Statement 1 is correct.

• The 44th Amendment (1978) provides that even during a National Emergency, the rights under Articles 20 (protection in respect of conviction) and 21 (life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended — Statement 2 is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Under Article 32, the Supreme Court can issue five writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto. High Courts have similar power under Article 226.

 

NOTE

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because both statements are factually true, making 'Both 1 and 2' the correct choice.

question: Under the 1991 New Economic Policy of India, the reduction of licensing restrictions and government controls on private industry is best described by which term?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Liberalisation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Liberalisation (उदारीकरण) refers to the removal or relaxation of government restrictions such as industrial licensing (the 'Licence Raj'), price controls, and entry barriers, giving private enterprise greater freedom.

• It was a core pillar of the 1991 LPG reforms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• The '1991 LPG reforms' = Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation. Privatisation = greater private ownership/disinvestment of PSUs; Globalisation = integrating the domestic economy with the world economy. The reforms were introduced under P.V. Narasimha Rao with Dr Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 (Privatisation) concerns ownership transfer; Option 3 (Globalisation) concerns global integration; Option 4 (Nationalisation) is the opposite (state takeover) — only Liberalisation describes removing licensing controls.

question:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option regarding Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Reserve Bank of India raises the repo rate to control high inflation.

Reason (R): A higher repo rate makes borrowing costlier for banks, which reduces the money supply in the economy.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks. Raising it is a standard tool to curb inflation — Assertion (A) is TRUE.

• A higher repo rate raises banks' borrowing costs, they in turn raise lending rates, credit demand falls, and money supply contracts — reducing inflationary pressure. This is exactly why the tool works, so Reason (R) is TRUE and correctly explains A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• The repo rate is decided by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC). Related tools: Reverse Repo Rate, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) and Open Market Operations (OMOs).

 

NOTE

• Option 2 is wrong because R does correctly explain A; Options 3 and 4 are wrong because both A and R are factually true.

question: What is the most distinctive feature of the 'Chhau' dance, performed in the Purulia and Seraikella styles of eastern India?
option_1: The rhythmic clapping of bamboo staves
option_2: The use of elaborate masks and martial, acrobatic movements
option_3: The balancing of pots on the head
option_4: The intricate hand mudras performed while seated
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'The use of elaborate masks and martial, acrobatic movements'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhau is a semi-classical dance combining martial, tribal and folk traditions; the Purulia (West Bengal) and Seraikella (Jharkhand) styles are famous for their large, colourful masks and vigorous, acrobatic movements. (The Mayurbhanj style of Odisha is performed without masks.)

• Chhau is inscribed on UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Chhau themes are often drawn from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and local legends. The three recognised styles are Purulia, Seraikella and Mayurbhanj.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 describes the Cheraw (bamboo) dance of Mizoram; Option 3 describes dances like Ghoomar/Bhavai balancing pots; Option 4 describes seated classical mudra-based forms — none is the defining feature of Chhau, which is its masks and martial movements.

question: Which of the following pairs of a local wind and its region is INCORRECTLY matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'Foehn – Sahara Desert'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Foehn is a warm, dry wind that blows on the leeward (northern) slopes of the Alps in Europe — NOT a Sahara Desert wind. Hence this pair is incorrectly matched.

• The hot, dust-laden Sahara-related winds are the Sirocco and the Harmattan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Correctly matched local winds: Loo – hot dry wind of northern India; Mistral – cold wind of France (Rhone valley); Chinook ('snow-eater') – warm wind of the Rocky Mountains; Sirocco – hot wind from the Sahara towards the Mediterranean.

 

NOTE

• Options 2 (Loo – Northern India), 3 (Mistral – France) and 4 (Chinook – Rockies) are all correctly matched, so they are not the answer; only the Foehn–Sahara pair is wrong, since the Foehn is an Alpine wind.
